english: I enrolled in university this semester.
grammar: 입학하다 (iphakada = to enroll) takes 에: 대학교에 입학해요 (daehakgyoe iphakaeyo).

english: Our university campus is really spacious.

target: 첫 수업이 아침 아홉 시에 시작해요.
english: The first class starts at nine in the morning.
grammar: 시 (si = o'clock) takes native numbers: 아홉 시 (ahop si = nine o'clock).

english: The professor gives lectures very interestingly.
grammar: 께서 (kkeseo) marks an honored subject and pairs with -세요: 교수님께서 하세요 (gyosunimkkeseo haseyo).

english: My sibling's lecture room is on the third floor.
grammar: 층 (cheung = floor) uses Sino numbers: 삼 층 (sam cheung = 3rd floor).

english: I major in business administration.
grammar: 전공하다 (jeongonghada = to major) takes 을/를: 경영학을 전공해요 (gyeongyeonghageul jeongonghaeyo).

english: My major is computer engineering.
grammar: 이에요/예요 = 'is': after a consonant 공학이에요 (gonghagieyo); after a vowel 친구예요 (chinguyeyo).

english: I'm taking six courses this semester.
grammar: 과목 (gwamok = course) counts with native numbers: 여섯 과목 (yeoseot gwamok = six courses).

english: My older brother finds his major classes hard.
My older sister likes the general-education classes.
I have as many as three classes today.
grammar: -이나 (-ina) means 'as many as': 세 개나 (se gaena = as many as three).

english: My older sister studies at the library until late at night.
During exam period there are no seats in the library.
I live in the dormitory.
I share my dorm room with a roommate.
grammar: 하고 (hago = with) joins people: 룸메이트하고 (rummeiteuhago = with a roommate).

english: Tuition goes up every year.
grammar: 마다 (mada = every) follows a noun: 해마다 (haemada = every year).

english: I really want to get a scholarship.
grammar: -고 싶다 = 'want to': 받고 싶어요 (batgo sipeoyo = want to receive).

english: I got a scholarship this time, so I'm really glad.
grammar: -아서/어서 links cause and result: 받아서 기뻐요 (badaseo gippeoyo = got it, so glad).

english: My sibling got a scholarship and is very happy.
grammar: 3rd-person feelings take -어해요: 기뻐해요 (gippeohaeyo = is glad), not 기뻐요.

english: The senior treats the juniors to a meal.
grammar: 한테 (hante) marks the receiver: 후배들한테 (hubaedeulhante = to the juniors).

english: The club meeting is on Friday evening.
grammar: 에 (e) marks a time: 저녁에 (jeonyeoge = in the evening).

english: I joined the photography club.
grammar: 가입하다 (gaipada = to join) takes 에: 동아리에 가입해요 (dongarie gaipaeyo).

english: The university festival opens next week.
A famous singer comes for the festival.
I'm going to Japan as an exchange student.
grammar: (으)로 marks a role: 교환 학생으로 (gyohwan haksaengeuro = as an exchange student).

english: Next year I'm going to study abroad in the US.
grammar: 유학을 가다 = 'to go study abroad': 유학을 가요 (yuhageul gayo).

english: Preparing for study abroad is really tough.
I prepare the visa documents in advance.
I need a foreign-language test score.
grammar: 필요하다 (piryohada = to need) takes 이/가: 점수가 필요해요 (jeomsuga piryohaeyo).

target: 저는 영어 실력을 더 키우고 싶어요.
english: I want to build up my English skills more.
I went on a language program for six months.
grammar: 개월 (gaewol = months) uses Sino numbers: 육 개월 (yuk gaewol = six months).

english: I made a lot of friends locally.
grammar: 사귀다 → 사귀었어요 (sagwieosseoyo = made friends), keeping 귀 before -었어요.

english: At first the classes were really hard.
Now I've gotten used to local life a lot.
grammar: -아/어지다 = 'become': 익숙해졌어요 (iksukhaejyeosseoyo = got used to).

english: My homestay family is really kind.
grammar: For elders, use honorific -세요: 친절하세요 (chinjeolhaseyo = is kind).

english: I come back to Korea during vacation.
Sometimes studying abroad feels lonely.
Learning new culture is really enjoyable.
My roommate is curious about my hometown.
grammar: 3rd-person curiosity takes -어해요: 궁금해해요 (gunggeumhaehaeyo = is curious).

target: 저는 여름 방학에 배낭여행을 갈 거예요.
english: I'll go backpacking this summer vacation.
grammar: -(으)ㄹ 거예요 = 'will': 갈 거예요 (gal geoyeyo = will go).

english: High schoolers prepare hard for the entrance exam.
The college entrance exam is in November.
grammar: Months use Sino numbers: 십일월 (sibirwol = November).

english: My older sister takes the entrance exam this year.
The exam hall is really quiet.
On exam day the whole country is tense.
My parents pray in front of the exam hall.
grammar: 께서 + -세요 mark honored parents as subject: 부모님께서 하세요 (bumonimkkeseo haseyo).

english: Colleges are decided by the exam score.
grammar: (으)로 marks the means: 점수로 (jeomsuro = by the score).

english: My sibling found the language section the hardest.
I couldn't solve a single math problem.
grammar: 하나도 + 못 = 'not a single one': 하나도 못 풀었어요 (hanado mot pureosseoyo).

english: After the exam I felt really relieved.
grammar: -고 = 'and then': 끝나고 (kkeunnago = it ends, and then).

english: There are many students who retake the year.
My sibling is stressed because of the exam.
grammar: 때문에 (ttaemune = because of) follows a noun: 수능 때문에 (suneung ttaemune).

english: My kid goes to the academy after school.

target: 형은 영어 학원에 삼 년 동안 다녔어요.
english: My older brother attended an English academy for three years.
grammar: 년 (nyeon = years) uses Sino numbers: 삼 년 (sam nyeon = three years).

target: 학원 수업이 밤 열 시에 끝나요.
english: The academy class ends at ten at night.
grammar: 시 uses native numbers: 열 시 (yeol si = ten o'clock).

target: 수학 학원 선생님께서 정말 잘 가르치세요.
english: The math academy teacher teaches really well.
grammar: honorific -세요 for the teacher: 가르치세요 (gareuchiseyo = teaches).

english: I send my child to piano academy.
grammar: 에 marks the destination: 학원에 보내요 (hagwone bonaeyo = send to the academy).

english: The academy fees are pricier than I thought.
grammar: 보다 (boda = than) marks comparison: 생각보다 (saenggakboda = than I thought).

target: 아들이 학원에서 단어 시험을 매일 봐요.
english: My son takes a vocab test at the academy every day.
My daughter takes online academy lectures.
Internet lectures are more convenient than the academy.
My son finds the academy homework hard.
grammar: 3rd-person feelings take -어해요: 힘들어해요 (himdeureohaeyo = finds it hard).

english: My sibling has midterms next week.
Finals are already coming up.
My older brother studied all night for the exam.
The range of this exam is too broad.

target: 동생이 이번 시험을 아주 잘 봤어요.
english: My sibling did really well on this exam.
grammar: 시험을 보다 = 'to take a test': 시험을 봤어요 (siheomeul bwasseoyo = took the test).

english: My grades went up from last semester.
grammar: 오르다 is 르-irregular: 올랐어요 (ollasseoyo = went up).

english: I showed my report card to my parents.
grammar: 께 (kke) is the honorific 'to': 부모님께 (bumonimkke = to my parents).

english: My sibling failed the exam and is upset.
I studied hard and passed the exam.
grammar: 시험에 붙다 = 'to pass a test': 붙었어요 (buteosseoyo = passed).

english: This time I'll definitely pass, I promise.
grammar: -(으)ㄹ게요 makes a promise: 합격할게요 (hapgyeokhalgeyo = I'll pass).

english: I'll prepare harder for the next exam, I promise.
The teacher announced the exam results.
grammar: honorific past -셨어요: 발표하셨어요 (balpyohasyeosseoyo = announced).

english: I'm preparing for a certification exam.
I applied for the Korean proficiency test.
grammar: 신청하다 (sincheonghada = to apply) takes 을/를: 시험을 신청해요 (siheomeul sincheonghaeyo).

english: My older sister missed the exam application period.
I want to raise my grades more.
I prepare the presentation together with my teammates.
I submitted the assignment by email.
grammar: (으)로 marks the means: 이메일로 (imeillo = by email).

english: The report deadline is until tomorrow.
grammar: 까지 (kkaji = until) marks a limit: 내일까지 (naeilkkaji = until tomorrow).

english: I pulled an all-nighter and finished the report.
The professor gives a lot of assignments.
grammar: honorific -세요 for the professor: 내세요 (naeseyo = gives out).

english: My older sister looks for presentation materials in the library.
I was so nervous when presenting.
grammar: -(으)ㄹ 때 = 'when': 발표할 때 (balpyohal ttae = when presenting).

english: I review together with my younger sibling.

target: 동생은 수업 전에 미리 예습을 해요.
english: My sibling previews before class.
I write hard words in my notebook.

target: 매일 새 단어를 열 개씩 외워요.
english: I memorize ten new words each day.
grammar: -씩 (-ssik) means 'each/apiece': 열 개씩 (yeol gaessik = ten each).

english: With the exam coming up I feel very nervous.
My sibling got touchy because of the exam.
The exams are all over, so I feel at ease.
My older brother's Korean grade is the best.
My sibling's math score dropped from last time.
The teacher explains the answers in detail.
grammar: honorific -세요: 설명하세요 (seolmyeonghaseyo = explains).

english: For problems I don't know, I ask the teacher.
grammar: 께 marks the honored receiver: 선생님께 (seonsaengnimkke = to the teacher).

english: I did well on the test so I feel good.
I hate group assignments the most.
My parents worry about my exam results.

target: 저는 방학 동안 인터넷 강의를 들을 거예요.
english: I'll take internet lectures over the vacation.
I met an elementary-school classmate after a long time.
In middle school I was class president.

target: 고등학교 삼 학년 때 진로를 정했어요.
english: I decided my career path in the third year of high school.
grammar: 학년 (hangnyeon = grade) uses Sino numbers: 삼 학년 (sam hangnyeon = 3rd grade).

english: My homeroom teacher was really nice.
grammar: honorific past -(으)셨어요: 좋으셨어요 (joeusyeosseoyo = was nice/good).

english: The students chatter in the classroom.
During break I go to the snack shop.
The school lunch was really tasty today.
My sibling gets along well with classmates.
My sibling dozed off in class and got scolded.
The teacher checks the homework carefully.
I commute to school by bus.
grammar: (으)로 marks the means: 버스로 (beoseuro = by bus).

english: During exams I'm short on sleep.
I set my goal for this semester.
Grades come out as much as you put in.
grammar: 만큼 (mankeum = as much as) follows a word: 노력한 만큼 (noryeokan mankeum = as much as you try).

english: When I grow up I want to become a teacher.
My sibling wants to become a scientist when they grow up.
grammar: 3rd-person wishes take -고 싶어해요: 되고 싶어해요 (doego sipeohaeyo = wants to become).

english: My parents cheer on my studies.
I'm really looking forward to the new semester.

target: 방학 숙제를 아직 다 못 했어요.
english: I still haven't finished all my vacation homework.
grammar: 못 + verb = 'cannot / didn't manage': 못 했어요 (mot haesseoyo = couldn't do).

english: The start of term is already next week.
My sibling makes the school newspaper.
The teacher helps with going on to higher school.
I transferred schools twice.
grammar: 번 (beon = times) uses native numbers: 두 번 (du beon = twice).

english: I attended an international school.

target: 좋은 대학에 가고 싶어서 정말 열심히 공부해요.
english: Because I want to get into a good university, I study really hard.
My father watches the news every morning.
grammar: 마다 (mada = every) follows a noun: 아침마다 (achimmada = every morning).

english: The news these days is so depressing.
I heard the news of that accident on the news.
My grandfather reads newspaper articles every day.
The reporter reports the incident in detail.
The news anchor speaks clearly.

target: 여행 전에 날씨 예보를 보고 우산을 챙겼어요.
english: Before the trip I checked the forecast and packed an umbrella.
grammar: -고 chains actions in order: 보고 챙겼어요 (bogo chaenggyeosseoyo = looked, then packed).

english: I'm very interested in economic news.
grammar: 관심이 많다 = 'be very interested': 관심이 많아요 (gwansimi manayo).

english: Political news is too complicated.
Breaking news suddenly popped up on the screen.
grammar: 뜨다 → 떴어요 (tteosseoyo = popped up); the ㅡ drops before -었어요.

english: I read overseas news on an app.
grammar: (으)로 marks the tool: 앱으로 (aebeuro = on an app).

english: There's a lot of fake news these days.
Online papers are faster than paper ones.
grammar: 보다 marks 'than': 종이 신문보다 (jongi sinmunboda = than paper papers).

english: I only read articles I'm interested in.
grammar: 만 (man = only) follows the noun: 기사만 (gisaman = only articles).

english: When I read news comments I get angry.
grammar: -(으)면 = 'when/if': 읽으면 (ilgeumyeon = when you read).

english: My sibling is on social media all day long.
My friend posted a new photo.
grammar: 올리다 → 올렸어요 (ollyeosseoyo = posted); 리 becomes 려 before -었어요.

english: I liked that post.
grammar: 누르다 → 눌렀어요 (nulleosseoyo = pressed): a 르-irregular.

english: People leave comments on my photos.
I have over a hundred followers.
grammar: 넘다 (neomda = to exceed) takes 이/가: 백 명이 넘어요 (baengmyeongi neomeoyo = over 100).

english: Popular posts have high view counts.
I often post photos of good restaurants.
I follow a famous influencer.

target: 저는 개인 정보를 온라인에 안 올려요.
english: I don't post personal info online.
grammar: 안 + verb = negation: 안 올려요 (an ollyeoyo = don't post).

english: I keep up with overseas friends' news through social media.

target: 저는 하루에 사진을 다섯 장 올려요.
english: I post five photos a day.
grammar: 장 (jang) counts flat things with native numbers: 다섯 장 (daseot jang = five sheets).

english: My sibling taps a heart on my photo.

target: 저는 SNS 계정이 두 개 있어요.
english: I have two social-media accounts.
grammar: 개 (gae) counts things with native numbers: 두 개 (du gae = two).

english: I changed my profile picture to a new one.
I switched my account to private.
grammar: (으)로 marks a change-into: 비공개로 (bigonggaero = into private).

english: A stranger sent a friend request.
I blocked that person right away.
grammar: 차단하다 (chadanhada = to block) takes 을/를: 사람을 차단해요 (sarameul chadanhaeyo).

english: There are really many people in the group chat.
We chat every day in the family group chat.
My grandmother leaves comments on my photos.
grammar: honorific -세요: 다세요 (daseyo = leaves/attaches).

english: My kid watches YouTube every night.
This YouTuber has a lot of subscribers.
I subscribed to that channel right away.
grammar: 구독하다 (gudokada = to subscribe) takes 을/를: 채널을 구독해요 (chaeneol-eul gudokaeyo).

english: When a new video is uploaded, a notification comes.
grammar: -(으)면 = 'when': 올라오면 (ollaomyeon = when it's uploaded).

english: My mother enjoys watching cooking videos.

target: 영상이 너무 길어서 두 배로 봐요.
english: The video is too long so I watch at double speed.
grammar: (으)로 marks the manner: 두 배로 (du baero = at double speed).

english: I binge-watched a drama on Netflix over the weekend.

target: 가족하고 주말에 영화를 세 편 봤어요.
english: I watched three movies with my family over the weekend.
grammar: 편 (pyeon) counts films with native numbers: 세 편 (se pyeon = three films).

english: This drama has five seasons.
grammar: 개 (gae) counts things with native numbers: 다섯 개 (daseot gae = five).

english: I'm really curious about the next episode.
My friend told me the drama's ending early.
My grandmother watches dramas with subtitles on.
This movie's picture quality is really good.
I download videos and watch them.
When ads come on I get really annoyed.
grammar: -(으)면 = 'when': 나오면 (naomyeon = when it comes out).

english: I look up videos of the singer I like.
grammar: 의 (ui) shows possession: 가수의 영상 (gasu-ui yeongsang = the singer's video).

target: 이 채널은 매주 새 영상을 올려요.
english: This channel posts new videos every week.
I study English on YouTube.
grammar: (으)로 marks the tool: 유튜브로 (yutyubeuro = via YouTube).

english: When I watch travel vlogs I want to leave.
grammar: -(으)면 = 'when': 보면 (bomyeon = when I watch).

english: I eat while watching mukbang.
grammar: -(으)면서 = 'while': 보면서 (bomyeonseo = while watching).

english: My sibling waits for the new webtoon every week.
This webtoon's art is really pretty.

target: 웹툰 한 편을 순식간에 다 봤어요.
english: I finished one webtoon episode in an instant.

target: 유료 웹툰은 미리 볼 수 있어요.
english: Paid webtoons you can view in advance.
grammar: -(으)ㄹ 수 있다 = 'can': 볼 수 있어요 (bol su isseoyo = can view).

english: My kid reads webtoons on a smartphone.
That webtoon was made into a drama.
grammar: (으)로 marks the result: 드라마로 (deuramaro = into a drama).

english: I was curious about the next episode, so I paid.
Popular webtoons have thousands of comments.
I want to become a webtoon artist.

target: 웹툰을 보면 시간이 정말 빨리 가요.
english: When I read webtoons, time really flies.
My mother does all her shopping on apps.
I ordered chicken on a delivery app.

target: 이 여행 앱은 정말 편하고 빨라요.
english: This travel app is really convenient and fast.
I installed a new app on my phone.
I updated the app to the latest version.

target: 해외에서 비밀번호를 잊어버려서 로그인을 못 했어요.
english: Abroad I forgot my password and couldn't log in.
I signed up for a travel app.
I find my way with a map app.
I booked a hotel with a travel app.

target: 번역 앱이 여행할 때 정말 유용해요.
english: A translation app is really useful when traveling.
grammar: -(으)ㄹ 때 = 'when': 여행할 때 (yeohaenghal ttae = when traveling).

english: I handle banking on an app.

target: 앱으로 택시를 부르면 정말 빨리 와요.
english: When you call a taxi with an app it comes really fast.
grammar: -(으)면 = 'when': 부르면 (bureumyeon = when you call).

english: I manage money with a budgeting app.

target: 운동 앱이 걸음 수를 세어 줘요.
english: A fitness app counts my steps.
I set my alarm for six o'clock.
grammar: 시 uses native numbers: 여섯 시 (yeoseot si = six o'clock).

english: I turned off all app notifications.
I save family photos to the cloud.

target: 여행 사진이 많아서 저장 공간이 부족해요.
english: I have so many travel photos that storage space is low.
I deleted all the old apps.
I back up family photos often.

target: 호텔 인터넷이 느려서 영상이 자꾸 멈춰요.
english: The hotel internet is slow so the video keeps stopping.
At the airport the wifi won't connect, so it's frustrating.
Abroad my data runs low, so I only use wifi.
My phone battery is already dead.
grammar: 다 되다 = 'be all used up': 다 됐어요 (da dwaesseoyo = is dead/empty).

english: I left my charger at the hotel.
grammar: -고 오다 = 'do and come': 두고 왔어요 (dugo wasseoyo = left it and came).

english: I lost my wireless earbuds during the trip.
I do video meetings on an app.
I use apps a lot while working from home.
grammar: -(으)면서 = 'while': 하면서 (hamyeonseo = while doing).

english: I take lectures online from abroad.

target: 저는 이메일을 하루에 스무 번 확인해요.
english: I check email twenty times a day.
grammar: 번 (beon = times) uses native numbers: 스무 번 (seumu beon = twenty times).

english: I accidentally deleted an important file.
grammar: (으)로 marks the cause here: 실수로 (silsuro = by mistake).

english: The app suddenly froze so I restarted it.
I don't answer unknown numbers.
Way too much spam texts come.

target: 저는 필요 없는 알림을 다 껐어요.
english: I turned off all the notifications I don't need.
I switched to a new phone and I'm really satisfied.

target: 아들이 게임 앱에 돈을 너무 많이 써요.
english: My son spends way too much money on game apps.

target: 아이가 게임을 너무 오래 해서 걱정돼요.
english: My kid plays games too long, so I'm worried.

target: 저는 아이의 스마트폰 사용 시간을 정해요.
english: I set my child's screen time.
My parents find using new apps difficult.
grammar: honorific of a 3rd-person feeling: 어려워하세요 (eoryeowohaseyo = find it hard).

english: I book train tickets on an app.
I got lost so I opened the map app.
Even abroad I watch Korean broadcasts on apps.
grammar: -도 (-do = even/also): 해외에서도 (haeoeseodo = even abroad).

english: I organize travel photos with an app.
Thanks to the interpreter app, the conversation was easy.
grammar: 덕분에 (deokbune = thanks to) follows a noun: 앱 덕분에 (aep deokbune = thanks to the app).

target: 저는 새 소식을 앱 알림으로 받아요.
english: I get new updates through app notifications.

target: 여행 앱에서 쿠폰을 받아서 싸게 샀어요.
english: I got a coupon on the travel app and bought it cheaply.

target: 저는 그 앱에 별점 오 점을 줬어요.
english: I gave that app five stars.
grammar: 점 (jeom = points) uses Sino numbers: 오 점 (o jeom = five points).

target: 여행 앱 후기를 꼼꼼히 읽고 골랐어요.
english: I read the travel app reviews carefully and chose.
My older sister listens to songs on a music app.
This app is free, so it's really nice.
grammar: 이다 connective -라서 = 'because it is': 무료라서 (muryoraseo = because it's free).

target: 여행 중에 매일 앱으로 일기를 써요.
english: During my trip I write a diary on an app every day.

target: 동생은 사진 앱으로 얼굴을 예쁘게 꾸며요.
english: My younger sibling prettifies their face with a photo app.

target: 어머니 병원 예약을 앱으로 잡아 드려요.
english: I book my mother's doctor appointment on an app for her.

target: 새로 나온 앱이 요즘 정말 인기예요.
english: A newly released app is really popular these days.
I screenshotted a photo of my kid and sent it to the family.
This app has no ads, so it's good.

target: 저는 앱 알림 소리를 진동으로 바꿨어요.
english: I changed the app alert sound to vibrate.

target: 화면이 자꾸 멈춰서 앱을 다시 깔았어요.
english: The screen kept freezing so I reinstalled the app.

target: 저는 하루에 휴대폰을 백 번 넘게 봐요.
english: I look at my phone over a hundred times a day.
